company.name: Coalesce.io
company.industry: Data transformation SaaS for the Snowflake ecosystem

routing_rationale: VP Engineering at a no-security-title company. Capacity-gap framing aimed precisely at the role's actual KPI: engineering-team time. The 'sprint tax' framing is engineering-leadership vernacular, not security vernacular.

research_summary.trigger_event: Same enterprise compliance pull as Satish; expressed as a hidden cost on engineering capacity rather than as a strategic question
research_summary.what_we_know: VP Eng at 130-person Snowflake-ecosystem company without dedicated security leader. Per craft/personas/vp-engineering.md, this role lives operationally and rewards observations grounded in the team's actual time.

draft.subject_line: SOC 2 evidence as a sprint tax
draft.body:
The cost of SOC 2 evidence at this stage rarely shows up as a line item — it's a tax on sprint capacity that would have gone to the platform. The shape we keep seeing at 130-person Snowflake-ecosystem companies is that the tax compounds quietly until enterprise renewal cycles make it visible, and by that point the option to absorb it has expired.

Transilience generates the evidence as a byproduct of how the platform runs — declared baseline, continuous drift detection, prioritized findings, remediation with humans in the loop — so the team's hours stay on the platform.

Worth fifteen minutes if I'm reading the shape right?
draft.architecture: diagnostic-pattern: the pattern is named ('sprint tax', 'compounds quietly until renewals'), the consequence stated, the alternative offered in one sentence

witness.what_works: 'Sprint tax' is a metaphor a VP Eng can feel. 'Compounds quietly until enterprise renewal cycles make it visible' is the diagnostic the role responds to per craft. The product sentence is one sentence, names the actual loop, and the closing 'team's hours stay on the platform' returns to the role's home metric (team time). No AI tells. Length is 4 sentences.
witness.what_fails: 'The shape we keep seeing' is a slightly generic vendor phrase — converts an opinion into an authority-claim. If signal is later found that I have not actually seen this 'shape' at multiple peer companies, this sentence becomes a credibility risk. Acceptable here because the pattern is genuinely common at this stage, but worth flagging as the first sentence to revise if the witness on the second pass tightens.

review_flags: coordinate-with-satish-jayanthi-coalesce: do not send same week — choose one as primary, one as secondary
